headline: Iraq Boosts Crude Oil Exports via Turkey Ceyhan Port to 500,000 Bpd
summary: Iraq has increased its crude oil exports through the Turkish Mediterranean port of Ceyhan to 500,000 barrels per day by trucking Basrah crude to the northern pipeline system.
why: Iraq is OPEC's second-largest oil producer, and changes in its export volumes can significantly impact global crude supply and international oil markets.

impacts.name: Brent crude
impacts.why: An increase in Iraqi oil exports expands global supply, which typically exerts downward pressure on crude prices.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: An increase in export volume from OPEC's second-largest producer expands physical supply availability in the market, putting downward pressure on prices.
